conventions.convention: Algebraic consistency means g(t0,x0,z0)=0. It need not imply consistency with a higher-index solution. Regular index one requires C1 data and invertible square g_z at a constraint zero.
The local differentiation index counts through the first derivative of the algebraic variable: the least positive differentiation count that regularly determines z and z'.
Residual-to-state control applies only inside the specified selected-branch balls, with uniform gamma, Lambda and rho; when Lambda>0, rho≤gamma/(sqrt(m) Lambda).

Backward-Euler derivative residual divides the differential update residual by h; constant-step BDF2 divides it by 2h. Algebraic residuals remain g(t,X,Z). Newton acceptance tests the concatenated scaled residual at tolerance 1.

Termination assumes returning exact-arithmetic primitives and counts explicit outer residual queries separately from Jacobian assembly and backend work. A root status certifies a residual tolerance, not an exact zero or discretization accuracy.
BDF2 accuracy uses a constant grid, N≥2, a C3 exact reduced solution, O(h²) starting errors and algebraic residuals, and O(h²) derivative and algebraic step residuals, all within the common tube.

load_bearing.statement: For Ck f,g on an open domain, k≥1, a constraint zero with invertible g_z has a unique local Ck branch z=ψ(t,x), with g=0 iff z=ψ, ψ_t=−g_z⁻¹g_t and ψ_x=−g_z⁻¹g_x. The reduced field F(t,x)=f(t,x,ψ(t,x)) is Ck, and solutions in the chart correspond exactly.

Under the stated common branch-ball, lower singular-value and anchored Jacobian bounds, with rho≤gamma/(sqrt(m) Lambda) when Lambda>0, every candidate in the specified ball satisfies ||z−ψ(t,x)||₂≤(2/gamma)||g(t,x,z)||₂ uniformly over the compact base set.
A semi-explicit DAE is x'=f(t,x,z), g(t,x,z)=0; algebraic consistency means g(t0,x0,z0)=0, and regular index one requires C1 data and invertible g_z at a constraint zero.

The index is the least positive integer k for which the original constraint and its first k differentiated equations locally determine z and z', with an invertible square Jacobian for the highest algebraic derivative.

With finite grids and Newton budget B and returning primitives, initialization and both steppers terminate. Initialization uses at most B+2 residual evaluations; S attempted steps use at most 1+S(B+2) for backward Euler and 2+S(B+2) for BDF2. Appended candidates satisfy their stated derivative and algebraic residual tolerances.

concerns.concern: Proof 1.1 asserts from componentwise Lagrange Taylor expansion that 'Each component remainder is at most (Lambda/2)||delta||₂².' The hypothesis bounds ||g_z(z)−G_*|| by Lambda||z−z_*|| only relative to the branch center; it does not directly bound Hessians at the Lagrange intermediate points. The claimed remainder estimate follows immediately by integrating (g_z(z_*+s delta)−G_*)delta over 0≤s≤1, but that justification is absent.
